2025 
 The Hon'Ble Shri Justice Anil Kumar Jukanti
 Criminal Petition No.7009 Of 2025
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (for short 'BNSS') by petitioner/accused No.3 to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.59 of 2024 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad.

entities.text: XIII Additional Chief Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against petitioner are under Sections 498A and 406 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short 'DP Act').
2. Heard Mr. K. Sai Babu, learned counsel for petitioner and Mr. Surepalli Prashanth, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1/State.
Perused the material on record.

3. On basis of a complaint filed by respondent No.2/de facto complainant, an FIR bearing No.513 of 2012 came to be registered on 22.11.2012 by the Central Crime Police Station, Hyderabad District,
for the offences punishable JAK, J CRLP_7009_2025 under Sections 498A and 406 of the IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the DP Act.
4.

entities.text: Central Crime Police Station, Hyderabad District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The gist of the complaint is that respondent No.2/de facto complainant married to Mr.
Naveeduddin Khan Uzair/accused No.1 on 14.02.2004 as per Muslim rites.
It is alleged that at the time of marriage, 12 tulas of gold, 4 tulas of silver, Rs.50,000 of cash and other household articles were given as dowry.
It is further alleged that from the date of marriage, her husband, her mother-in-law and her husband's younger brother used to torture her physically and mentally for not bringing enough dowry.
There is an allegation that her husband used to consume liquor and ganja and beat her.
It is further alleged that her husband used to threaten her that he would marry for second time.
5. It is alleged in the complaint that respondent No.2's mother-in-law, who used to stay in United States, would call her and abuse her in filthy language and tortured her mentally and physically.
That the verbal abuse of her mother-in-law caused respondent No.2 severe mental agony and physical pain.
It is further alleged that an amount of JAK, J CRLP_7009_2025 Rs.1,00,000/- was given as additional dowry to her husband.
That during the time of respondent No.2's delivery, her husband performed second marriage in the month of June, 2010 and cheated her.

6. It is alleged that accused No.1's second wife was working in an international school and it is only for the purpose of money, accused No.1 married Saima Abrar (second wife) and thereby cheated her as well.
That due to mental torture, cruelty, harassment and physical abuse by her husband,
husband's younger brother,
coupled with the fact of second marriage, respondent No.2 obtained Khula on 05.12.2010 and since then she was staying in her parent's house.

That after Khula,

sentences.text: 7. It is further alleged that accused No.1/husband of respondent No.2 would visit respondent No.2's place and used to request her to remarry.
Ultimately, respondent No.2 agreed for remarriage.

Accused No.1 promised respondent No.2 that he would give divorce to Saima Abrar (his 2nd wife)
and on 16.08.2012, respondent No.2 remarried accused No.1 JAK, J CRLP_7009_2025 at Qazaath Office, Shah Ali Banda, Hyderabad.
That respondent No.2's mother-in-law arrived in Hyderabad on 15.08.2012 and she promised respondent No.2 to look after her and children welfare.
After remarriage, her husband's attitude became harsher.
That her mother-in-law and her husband's younger brother also started to torture her and that she and her children were not provided with nutritious food, causing them to become weak.
Hence, the complaint.
8. A charge sheet came to be filed and it also reflects the same.
9. CC.No.34 of 2014 came to be heard and was dismissed by XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, by an order dated 05.02.2025.

entities.text: XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The operative portion of the order is as follows:
"24. PW5 specifically admitted that she did not file any proof before Court to show that they received receipts of gold and silver ornaments.
The prosecution fails to prove that the accused harassed PW1 for demanding Additional Dowry.
As discussed Supra the prosecution fails to prove guilty of A1 A2 under Section 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
25. In the above facts and circumstances there is no evidence on record for establishing the guilt of Accused A1 and A2 as they committed the offence as alleged by prosecution.
So, the prosecution misarably fails to prove the guilty of Accused A1 and A2 beyond JAK, J CRLP_7009_2025 all reasonable doubt.
Case against A3 is Split up and given new C.C.59/2024 and same is pending.

26. In the result, the accused A1 and A2 are found not guilty for the offence punishable U/S 498- A, 406 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act the accused nos.1 and A2 are acquitted U/s. 248(1) Cr.P.C.

The bail bonds of the accused nos.1 and A2 shall stands cancelled after six months."
10.
Case against petitioner/accused No.3 was split up and renumbered as CC.No.59 of 2024.

When this Court queried learned counsel as to why the case was split up, it was stated across the Bar that petitioner/accused No.3 was residing in Australia, for the purpose of job/studies and as such, it was split up.

11. Learned counsel for petitioner placed reliance on the order of the trial Court and submitted that the trail Court held that accused Nos.1 and 2 were found not guilty for the offences under Sections 498A and 406 of the IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the DP Act.

That as the complaint is same, FIR and charge sheet also same, the charges against petitioner/accused No.3 be quashed i.e., the proceedings Nadeemuddin Khan vs The State Of Telangana on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161301734/

entities.text: Additional Chief Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submitted that it is borne by record that CC.No.34 of 2014 on the file of XIII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad,
is dismissed stating that accused Nos.1 and 2 were found not guilty for the offences under the Sections 498A and 406 of the IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the DP Act.

entities.text: XIII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: That for accused No.3 the case was split up for the very same offences and case was renumbered as CC.No.59 of 2024.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor further submitted that the case against petitioner/accused No.3 be permitted to go on, as there are allegations against him.
13. Heard learned counsels, perused the record and considered rival submissions.
14. On last occasion, this Court directed learned Assistant Public Prosecutor to serve notice on respondent No.2.
To that extent a memo has been filed by the Office of Public Prosecutor stating that notice was sent to respondent No.2.
JAK, J CRLP_7009_2025

In the notice dated 17.07.2025, it is reflected that mother of respondent No.2 was residing at the said residential address and she had received the copy of notice and has endorsed that respondent No.2 is in Saudi Arabia and that they are not in contact.

In other words,
there is no form of empowerment to prosecute the case, further, of the like of Special Vakalth Holder.
15. Be that as it may, this Court has perused the complaint, FIR, charge sheet and the record.
No specific allegations are levelled against petitioner/accused No.3.
No allegations are forthcoming about the active involvement of petitioner/accused No.3.
No particularized allegations are borne from the record.

Court of Competent Jurisdiction for the same set of allegations against accused Nos.1 and 2 in CC.No.34 of 2014 by its order dated 05.02.2025 held that accused Nos.1 and 2 are found not guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 of the IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the DP Act.

As the proceedings in the present criminal petition arise out of the same FIR and charge sheet and as there are no specific allegations against JAK, J CRLP_7009_2025 petitioner/accused No.3, the proceedings against petitioner/accused No.3 are liable to be quashed.
16. For reasons aforesaid, proceedings against petitioner/accused No.3 in C.C.No.59 of 2024 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad, are hereby quashed.

entities.text: XIII Additional Chief Magistrate, Mahila Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 17. Accordingly, the criminal petition is allowed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
